line: The task and versioned prompt go to a bounded coding agent (trial.py) that calls an external model through an OpenRouter client with a spending ledger; that client is built and tested offline only, with no live call yet. The agent runs agent-authored development checks (run_checks.py) in fresh Podman containers (sandbox.py, worker.py), which hold only candidate code. An explicit final submission passes source validation (contract.py) and separate hidden acceptance grading (evaluate.py), whose expected answers and scoring stay outside candidate containers. Results go to local run bundles (bundle.py, run_recording.py), which feed grading replay (replay.py) and local MLflow recording (mlflow_tracking.py, so far only a fixture bundle recorded against the local service). Comparison metrics are computed from the bundles, not read back from MLflow (comparison.py; experiment.py writes the bundles). The tooling is built offline but no comparison has run, so reviewed Markdown summaries of results are pending. Deterministic CI covers fixtures and probes and reaches the report through the reviewed CI evidence page, and the report builder (scripts/build_work_log.py) turns selected Markdown into the local report. Solid blue boxes are implemented; solid yellow boxes are partly implemented with no live or real run yet; dashed boxes are pending.

The current implementation is still an offline pilot: it loads three tasks and twelve cases, validates Python source, executes one case at a time in a restricted Podman container, and scores returned values outside that container. The agent loop, OpenRouter client (offline only), bundles/replay, the ten-task benchmark, CI, MLflow recording, and the comparison tooling are implemented on `main`; no live model run or comparison result exists yet. The offline HTML work-log builder exists (see below). Local orchestration will run on the laptop with uv; MLflow and disposable candidate execution use Podman. Complete the local loop before CI/tracking integration.
These fixtures verify controller behaviour (tool handling, limits, stopping, classification). They do not measure live model quality; there is no live client yet.
